slides.title: Tree Terminology

blocks.text: There is only one root node in the tree that appears at the top level of the tree and that has no parent node.
Nodes at a lower level of a tree are the children of nodes that appear at the previous level. For example, B, C, and D are the children of the parent node A.
An internal node should have at least one child node. For example, B is an internal node.
A node that has no children is called a leaf node.
Nodes that have the same parent are called siblings. For example, E and F are sibling nodes.

slides.title: More Tree Terminology

blocks.text: We can follow a path through a tree from a node at an upper level to a node at a lower level.
For example, the path from A to J is A → D → G → J.
The path length is the number of edges followed. For example, the path length from A to J is 3.
The level of a node is the length of the path from the root to the node. For example, the level of node G is 2.
The height of a tree is the length of the longest path from the root to a leaf node. The height of our example tree is 3.

slides.title: Degree of a Tree

blocks.text: A tree can be classified according to the maximum number of children any node in the tree may have.
The degree of a tree is the maximum number of children that any node in the tree can have.
A binary tree has a degree of 2 (at most 2 children per node)
A ternary tree has a degree of 3 (at most 3 children per node)
A k-ary tree has a degree of k (at most k children per node)
A general tree has no limit to the number of children nodes.

slides.title: Balanced versus Unbalanced Trees

blocks.text: A tree is balanced if all the leaf nodes are on the same level or within one level of each other.
The tree remains balanced in height to maintain efficient operations such as search, insertion, and deletion.

slides.title: Complete and Full Trees

blocks.text: A k-ary tree is complete if each level l has the maximum number of nodes kl, except for the last level in which all the nodes appear to the left side of the tree. If the last level of the tree is also complete, then the tree becomes full.

slides.title: Array Implementation of a Binary Tree

blocks.text: An array is used to store all the tree elements.
There is no left and right pointer to a child node.
The root element starts at index 0.
If a tree element appears at index i, then its left child will be at index 2i + 1 and its right child will be at index 2i + 2.
The array implementation of a binary tree is very effective.
The array capacity can be expanded like an array list.

slides.title: Tree Traversals

blocks.text: For a linear structure, such as a list, the process of iterating through the elements is simple (forward or backward).
For a tree structure, there are more choices for tree traversal.
Each node in the tree becomes the root of a subtree.
There are four basic methods for traversing a tree:
Preorder Traversal
Inorder Traversal
Postorder Traversal
Level-order Traversal

public TreeNode<T> find(T target) {

// If found then return reference to this node object
  if (element.equals(target)) return this;

TreeNode<T> node = null;
                                    // If target not found

// Recursively search the left subtree
  if (left != null) node = left.find(target);

// If not found in left subtree, then search right subtree
  if (node == null && right != null) node = right.find(target);

return node;
}
